text:
nightly-bot: :rotating_light: Nightdash alert: p95 latency for streaming-inference route increased 2.8x in the last 12h. Investigate. dashboard: https://nightdash/internal/redwood/runtime

olivia: saw this at 03:12 too. p50 ~48ms -> 85ms, p95 ~120ms -> 340ms. throughput steady.

prasanna: sounds like a batching heuristic regression to me. any recent rollout that touched batch window or kernel selector?

olivia: dedicated deploy rolled v1.24.0 to canary at 00:45, full rollout at 01:30. commit bae3f9c rolled in PR #1482.

devon: copying CI perf job output (trimmed):
```
perf-nightly/batching: p95 latency (tokens/sec) baseline=45ms new=135ms diff=+200%
profiler snapshot: kernel_select_time +3.2ms, kv_cache_evictions +6.1x
```

lena: KV metrics look bad: evictions/sec jumped 200 -> 1400, kv-miss-rate 7% -> 39% after rollout window. memory usage on pods spiked ~1.2GB.

aaron: @prasanna can you bisect the rollout range? my hunch is the adaptive batching refactor.

prasanna: starting quick bisect locally. suspect range: v1.23.4..v1.24.0. using: `git bisect start -- bad bae3f9c good v1.23.4`

prasanna: found candidate commit 7c2f1b9 (batching: adjust async window + kernel heuristics). Reproducer on dev: run `./scripts/run-nightdash --model gpt-small --load-profile nightly/2026-03-15` gives p95 ~320ms.

devon: ran pprof on the reproducer, flame summary:
```
8.7%  kernel_selector.cpp:select_best_kernel
6.4%  batching/scheduler.cpp:try_merge_windows
5.9%  kv_cache/evictor.cpp:evict_if_needed
```

olivia: interesting — kernel_selector time up and evictor doing more work. maybe batching changed request shapes causing worse cache locality.

lena: if cache thrash is driving recompute latency, we should mitigate by tightening cache retention or lowering async batch window. can we push a config rollback first?

aaron: I'll stage a canary rollback to 1.23.8 (last stable with green nightly). rolling to canary now.

eng-sre-bot: deploy triggered: canary -> infra-runtime/us-west-2 (deployment id: deploy-3821).

nightly-bot: CI perf job re-run on canary rollback queued.

prasanna: while rollback runs, I pushed a small patch to reduce async_batch_window default from 40ms -> 20ms as a short-term guard: PR #1497.

devon: quick numbers from canary after rollback: p95 down to ~130ms (still slightly above baseline). KV evictions back to ~220/sec. memory normalized.

olivia: sounds like the rollback helped. leave PR #1497 as hotfix until we can do deeper root cause.

prasanna: next steps: full bisect on the batching refactor to isolate kernel-selection interaction, add unit test for KV locality patterns, add perf test in CI reproducing the 50-token hot-path.

lena: opening incident ticket with notes + links to profiler outputs and canary rollout steps. assigning to eng-runtime.

aaron: marking rollout blocked and paused in release board until PR #1482 is reverted in prod.

eng-sre-bot: incident updated: INCIDENT-2026-032 - runtime p95 spike. status: mitigated (canary rollback). monitoring retained.

nightly-bot: closing alert thread automatically after 10m of stable metrics.

olivia: thanks everyone. follow-up: schedule 2h deep-dive tomorrow with kernel selection owners and perf infra. :calendar:
